name: Differentiable Ocean Inverse Modeling
aliases: Ocean surface reconstruction via differentiable rendering
definition: A two-step framework to reconstruct dynamic ocean models from monocular video sequences. Step 1: Reconstruct hierarchical geometry (macrosurface normal and microfacet roughness) from images using encoder-decoder networks. Step 2: Estimate component wave parameters (amplitude, frequency, direction) from the geometric sequences using an MLP. The process is self-supervised using a differentiable renderer and a differentiable ocean model as loss functions.
summary: Differentiable Ocean Inverse Modeling reconstructs dynamic ocean models from monocular video by using a differentiable renderer and model as self-supervised loss functions to enable gradient-based optimization.
